packet.headline_seed: Five Italians die during cave dive in Maldives
packet.description_seed: Italy says the incident happened at a depth of 50m. Maldivian rescuers have so far found one body.

what: Five Italians die during cave dive in Maldives

clean_source_blocks.text: Five Italians have died in a scuba diving accident in the Maldives, the foreign ministry in Rome has said. "The divers are believed to have died while attempting to explore caves at a depth of 50 metres (164ft)," the ministry said, adding that this happened in Vaavu Atoll. The Maldives' military said one body had been found in a cave about 60 metres underwater, and the other four divers were believed to be also there. It said divers with special equipment had been sent to the area, describing a search operation as a very high risk. The incident is believed to be the worst single diving accident in the tiny Indian Ocean nation, a popular tourist destination because of its string of coral islands. The five Italians entered the water on Thursday morning, local media reported.
Italy says the incident happened at a depth of 50m. Maldivian rescuers have so far found one body.

Five Italian scuba divers have died after vanishing during a deep cave dive in the Maldives. Authorities are calling the incident, which took place in the Vaavu Atoll, one of the worst recent diving tragedies, as the five tourists attempted to explore underwater caves at a depth of approximately 165 feet, according to Italy's Foreign Ministry, on Thursday (May 14). One of the victims is believed to be a researcher from Genoa, reports Il Sole 24 Ore. The five victims were aboard the Duke of York, according to Maldivian outlet The Edition, which was operated by foreign staff, and went missing during a dive near Arimathea.

Five Italian nationals have died while scuba diving ‌in the Maldives, sparking an investigation by local police. The victims have been named by Italian media as university professor Monica Montefalcone and her 20-year-old daughter Giorgia Sommacal. Muriel Oddenino from Turin was also killed in the tragedy along with Gianluca Benedetti from Padua, and Federico Gualtieri from Borgomanero, according to local reports. The incident occurred in Vaavu Atoll, where the ⁠group had been attempting to explore underwater caves at a depth of around 165ft, Italy's foreign ministry said on Thursday. It did not give any ⁠details about the exact cause of the incident. Rescue crews raced to the area at around 1.45pm local time after the group vanished. According to Maldivian outlet The Edition, the group were tourists and had been aboard the Duke of York liveaboard diving vessel.

original_article.research:
[Lähde: BBC World]
Five Italians have died in a scuba diving accident in the Maldives, the foreign ministry in Rome has said.

"The divers are believed to have died while attempting to explore caves at a depth of 50 metres (164ft)," the ministry said, adding that this happened in Vaavu Atoll.

The Maldives' military said one body had been found in a cave about 60 metres underwater, and the other four divers were believed to be also there.

It said divers with special equipment had been sent to the area, describing a search operation as a very high risk.

The incident is believed to be the worst single diving accident in the tiny Indian Ocean nation, a popular tourist destination because of its string of coral islands.

The five Italians entered the water on Thursday morning, local media reported.

The crew of the diving vessel they were travelling on reported them missing when they failed to resurface later on.

Police said the weather was rough in the area, about 100km (62 miles) south of the capital Malé. A yellow warning was issued for passenger boats and fishermen.

The University of Genoa later said the victims included a marine biology professor, her daughter and two young researchers.

In a statement on X, the university expressed its "deepest condolences" to the victims.

Diving and snorkelling accidents are relatively rare in the Maldives, although several fatalities have been reported in recent years.

Last December, an experienced British female diver drowned in a scuba incident off the island resort of Ellaidhoo. Her husband died five days later after falling ill.

In 2024, a Japanese lawmaker died while snorkelling in Lhaviyani Atoll.

---

[Lähde: The Mirror]
Five Italian nationals have died while scuba diving ‌in the Maldives, sparking an investigation by local police.

The victims have been named by Italian media as university professor Monica Montefalcone and her 20-year-old daughter Giorgia Sommacal. Muriel Oddenino from Turin was also killed in the tragedy along with Gianluca Benedetti from Padua, and Federico Gualtieri from Borgomanero, according to local reports.

The incident occurred in Vaavu Atoll, where the ⁠group had been attempting to explore underwater caves at a depth of around 165ft, Italy's foreign ministry said on Thursday. It did not give any ⁠details about the exact cause of the incident.

Rescue crews raced to the area at around 1.45pm local time after the group vanished.

According to Maldivian outlet The Edition, the group were tourists and had been aboard the Duke of York liveaboard diving vessel.

The outlet reports that the group went missing during a dive near Alimathaa. They had entered the water in the morning and were reported missing by crew after failing to resurface.

Local police have launched a probe into the incident, with the causes of death yet to be confirmed.

A yellow weather warning had been issued in Vaavu Atoll earlier in the day and still remains in place as strong winds lashed the islands at up to 30mph.

Weather conditions at the dive site were reportedly poor at the time of the incident.

The ministry said an investigation had been launched by Maldivian authorities. It added that the Italian Embassy in Sri Lanka is in contact with the victims' families to provide consular assistance.

---

[Lähde: ITIJ]
Five Italian nationals have died following a scuba diving accident in the Maldives, Italy’s foreign ministry has confirmed.

The incident took place in Vaavu Atoll, where the group was reportedly exploring underwater caves at depths of around 50 metres (165ft). An investigation is underway into the circumstances of the accident.

The Italian foreign ministry said its embassy in Sri Lanka is providing consular support and assisting families.

While details remain limited, the case highlights the ongoing exposure faced by travel insurers and assistance providers in managing claims linked to high-risk leisure and expedition activities, particularly in remote locations.

Diving incidents of this nature can quickly escalate into complex international assistance cases, requiring coordination across local emergency services, specialist medical teams, and cross-border repatriation pathways – often from jurisdictions with limited hyperbaric or critical care infrastructure.

The Editorial Team updates the ITIJ website daily, and works on features for the print edition. With expert industry knowledge and years of experience in writing about complex travel insurance issues, the Editorial Team is ready to investigate and report on the topics that matter most to ITIJ's readers.

---

[Lähde: Irish Mirror]
Five Italian scuba divers have died after vanishing during a deep cave dive in the Maldives.

Authorities are calling the incident, which took place in the Vaavu Atoll, one of the worst recent diving tragedies, as the five tourists attempted to explore underwater caves at a depth of approximately 165 feet, according to Italy's Foreign Ministry, on Thursday (May 14).

One of the victims is believed to be a researcher from Genoa, reports Il Sole 24 Ore. The five victims were aboard the Duke of York, according to Maldivian outlet The Edition, which was operated by foreign staff, and went missing during a dive near Arimathea.

The group entered the water early in the morning but failed to resurface, prompting the crew to raise the alarm shortly before midday. Conditions at the dive site were said to be poor at the time.

Italy’s foreign ministry, together with the embassy in Colombo, is supporting the victims’ families, while Maldivian officials have opened an investigation into the incident.

payload.title: Viisi italialaista kuoli luolasukelluksella Malediiveilla
payload.summary: Viisi italialaista sukeltajaa on kuollut Malediiveilla Vaavun atollilla. Italian ulkoministeriön mukaan ryhmä oli tutkimassa vedenalaisia luolia noin 50 metrin syvyydessä.
payload.content:
Viisi italialaista sukeltajaa on kuollut Malediiveilla Vaavun atollilla tapahtuneessa onnettomuudessa, Italian ulkoministeriö kertoi torstaina. Ministeriön mukaan ryhmä oli ilmeisesti tutkimassa vedenalaisia luolia noin 50 metrin syvyydessä, kun onnettomuus tapahtui.

## Sukeltajat katosivat syvällä luola-alueella

Malediivien armeijan mukaan yksi ruumis on löydetty luolasta noin 60 metrin syvyydestä. Neljän muun sukeltajan uskotaan olevan samalla alueella. Viranomaisten mukaan paikalle on lähetetty erikoisvarustein toimivia sukeltajia, ja etsintäoperaatiota on kuvattu erittäin riskialttiiksi.

Paikallisten tietojen mukaan viisi italialaista meni veteen torstaiaamuna. Pelastusryhmät hälytettiin alueelle noin kello 13.45 paikallista aikaa sen jälkeen, kun ryhmä oli kadonnut sukelluksen aikana. Onnettomuuden tarkkaa syytä ei ole kerrottu julkisuuteen.

## Ryhmä oli sukellusaluksella Vaavun atollilla

Lähdetietojen mukaan sukeltajat olivat Duke of York -nimisellä liveaboard-sukellusaluksella, jota operoi ulkomainen henkilökunta. Ryhmä katosi sukelluksella Arimathean lähellä Vaavun atollilla. Malediivit tunnetaan korallisaaristaan ja sukelluskohteistaan, ja tapausta on kuvattu yhdeksi saarivaltion vakavimmista yksittäisistä sukellusonnettomuuksista.

Italian mediassa uhreiksi on nimetty yliopiston professori Monica Montefalcone ja hänen 20-vuotias tyttärensä Giorgia Sommacal. Lisäksi kuolleiksi on raportoitu Muriel Oddenino Torinosta, Gianluca Benedetti Padovasta ja Federico Gualtieri Borgomanerosta. Yhden uhrin on kerrottu olleen Genovasta kotoisin oleva tutkija.

Paikallispoliisin kerrotaan selvittävän tapahtumien kulkua. Tähän mennessä vahvistettuja tietoja ovat uhrien määrä, onnettomuuden sijainti Vaavun atollilla sekä se, että sukeltajat olivat noin 50 metrin syvyydessä vedenalaisissa luolissa.
summary_bullets: Viisi italialaista sukeltajaa kuoli Malediiveilla Vaavun atollilla.
Italian ulkoministeriön mukaan ryhmä oli tutkimassa vedenalaisia luolia noin 50 metrin syvyydessä.
Malediivien viranomaiset ovat löytäneet yhden ruumiin ja pitävät etsintäoperaatiota erittäin riskialttiina.
payload.journalist_note: Perustuu useiden lähteiden yhteneviin tietoihin onnettomuuden paikasta, uhrien määrästä ja sukelluksen luonteesta. Uhrien nimet on esitetty varauksella, koska ne ovat lähdetietojen mukaan italialaismedian raportoimia.
